messages.author: eb80836d4b6deddb
messages.subject: BLUP and BLUE estimation
parts:
Hi team

I am a bit confused by syntax to get BLUP values with spde model, for example:

 linharange= range(dat$linha,na.rm=T)
    colunarange= range(dat$coluna,na.rm=T)
   
    bordas=data.frame(x=c(colunarange[1],colunarange[2],colunarange[2],colunarange[1],colunarange[1]),
                         y=c(linharange[1],linharange[1],linharange[2],linharange[2],linharange[1]))
    #mp= max(max(dat$linha),max(dat$coluna))*0.05
    mesh= inla.mesh.2d(loc=dat[,c('coluna','linha')],
                         loc.domain=bordas,
                         offset=c(5,15),#mp*0.1
                         max.edge=c(4,6),#mp
                         cutoff=c(1))#mp
    spde= inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh,alpha=2)
    A=inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh,loc=as.matrix(dat[,c('coluna','linha')]))
    stk.e=inla.stack(tag='est',data=list(peso=dat$peso),
                        A=list(A,1,1,1),
                        effects=list(field=1:spde$n.spde,
                                     clone=as.factor(dat$clone),
                                     linha=dat$linha,
                                     coluna=dat$coluna))

m2spde=inla(formula = as.formula(fspde),  data = inla.stack.data(stk.e),
                 control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.e)),num.threads = 2)

BLUPspde= m2spde$summary.random$clone
BLUPspde


If I remove the num.threads each time I turn on the model, the BLUP values is very different and this difference is very large (file attached). By contrast if I leave num.threads and, its values is greather than 1 there are a large difference in the BLUP values for each time I turn on the model. So, what is the function of num.threads in the analysis? And how can i solve the change in the BLUP values? Too why the BLUP values estimated by spde (INLA) is lower in comparation with the values obtained by lme4?


Another question is related to BLUE values estimation. Why some BLUE values are negative  (file attached)?Because I used the idea with AR1, and I didn't have negative values. I used this lines of programation:

fspde=peso~  -1+ f(field,model=spde)+ clone

m2spde=inla(formula = as.formula(fspde),  data = inla.stack.data(stk.e),
                 control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.e)),num.threads = 2)

BLUEspde= m2spde$summary.fixed
BLUEspde

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] BLUP and BLUE estimation
parts:
make sure to use the most recent testing version and (enable PARDISO if
you're using Linux/Mac, see inla.pardiso())

I guess the model is almost singular, hence the posterior is 'almost
flat'. you can improve this using the new code,

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(inla.mode="experimental")

and you may also add, if you need to

r <- inla(....)
r <- inla.rerun(r)

although this *should* not be needed, but you can check. let me know...

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] BLUP and BLUE estimation
parts:
the small changes are due to the parallel computations

I see you have turned off the intercept term, hence it will be captured
in the spde term (likely). so if you're data is far from mean zero, then
the range will be elevated due to this.

you can make sure the above will happen, adding

f(clone, model="iid", constr=TRUE)

which will force this term to sum-to-zero
